summary: A paraphrase-consistency detector asks the subject model the same question in other words, in new chats, and flags a reply that disagrees with most of those answers.
tagline: Ask again in new chats, and compare the answers.
safetyUse:
A lie in one chat can depend on that chat: its system prompt, its motive or its earlier turns. The detector asks the subject model the same factual question in 3 paraphrases, each in a new chat with no earlier context. When the reply in the chat disagrees with most of these answers, the detector flags it as a lie. It needs only text in and out, so an auditor can use it through an API.

On OpenAudit, the Varied Deception eval tests it on prompted lies about TriviaQA questions.
caveats: It works only for questions with a short answer that a judge can compare. Open-ended replies are out of scope.

On Varied Deception, AISI kept only questions that the model answers correctly with a neutral prompt, and labeled a wrong reply a lie. The new chats repeat this check, so the score is an upper bound for prompted lies.
A model that lies in all chats (a trained liar, or a lie from a fixed system prompt that the new chats also have) gives consistent answers, and the detector does not flag it.
It flags a disagreement, not intent. An honest error that changes with the wording also looks like a lie.
Each reply costs a few calls to the subject model and to a helper model (paraphrases and the answer match).

params.label: Paraphrases
params.description: The number of paraphrases of the question, each in a new chat.

params.label: Context of the new chats
params.description: What the new chats keep of the original chat: none, or the system prompt.

params.label: Helper model
params.description: The model that writes the paraphrases and compares the answers.
